fullPassage:
Multisensory experiences are a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted, especially when our senses function normally or are corrected to normal with aids like glasses.

(A) And it does not stop there. Even the sounds that come both from the atmospheres in which we eat and our interactions with the food (such as chewing) and the tools we use to eat influence our eating experience.

(B) However, closer inspection to any, even the most ordinary experiences, reveals the remarkable multisensory world in which we live. Consider the experience of eating a regular meal.

(C) At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses. We first eat with our eyes, but we are also exposed to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food textures, tastes, and smells.

questions.passage: (A) And it does not stop there. Multisensory experiences ①<u>are</u> a central part of our everyday lives, yet we often take them for granted. However, closer inspection to any experiences reveals the remarkable multisensory world. At first, it may seem like an ordinary experience, but it is actually a fusion of the senses. We first eat with our eyes, but we are also ②<u>exposing</u> to countless sensory signals that influence our eating experience such as food ③<u>textures</u>, tastes, and ④<u>smells</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ② exposing → exposed: 'be exposed to'(~에 노출되다) 수동태. 주어(we)가 노출'되는' 것이므로 과거분사 exposed
✅ ① are: 복수 주어 experiences와 일치
✅ ③ textures: 복수 명사 정상
✅ ④ smells: 복수 명사 정상
det.tip: be exposed to = ~에 노출되다 (수동). be exposing to(×)

✅ ① them: 앞의 multisensory experiences(복수) 대명사 정상
✅ ③ in which: 전치사+관계대명사 정상 (= where)
✅ ④ eating: 전치사 of 뒤 동명사 정상

✅ ② that: sounds를 선행사로 한 주격 관계대명사 정상

❌ ④ what → the atmospheres in which: 원문은 'the atmospheres in which we eat'(우리가 먹는 분위기)이므로 what은 부정확. what we eat = 우리가 먹는 것(음식)으로 의미가 달라짐
